object_description: two equal-depth buildings with contrasting facade expressions
design_condition: Two buildings continue the surrounding rhythm while leaving two unhierarchical gaps, forming a minimally equipped courtyard and a publicly oriented roof space.

positive.statement: The two buildings continue the heterogeneous character of the district through contrasting expressions.
The public sports field on the roof is a welcome approach to expanding publicly usable space vertically.
The division into sports and school buildings is functionally and operationally conceivable.
The classroom floors are organized advantageously with generous access and a clear structure.
The classrooms are well proportioned and the main entrances are immediately legible.
The efficient supporting structure makes the flow of forces tangible and resolves the earthquake bracing very well.
Compactness, durable materials, and system separation support good energy and life-cycle performance.

negative.statement: The sports centre creates two similarly wide gaps without a clear hierarchy.
The most expressive facade faces the neighbour and is only visible from the corner, while parking reduces its impact.
It remains unclear whether the connecting material is sufficient to read the two buildings as an ensemble.
The courtyard infrastructure is minimal and the outdoor space is reduced largely to circulation, limiting its quality of stay.
The roof sports field places high demands on operation and use and depends on a very clear access solution.
The required open-space ratio is not met, even with the roof sports field.
The ground-floor arrangement limits possibilities for spatial demarcation too much.
The mobile separation of preparation and collection rooms does not adequately meet operational requirements and impairs openness when closed.
The high proportion of glass in the sports halls limits usability.
The open staircase cannot serve as an escape route and would require extensive fire-protection equipment and an additional stair.
The building depth and indeterminate setting are strange in this context, and the resulting small courtyard cannot be adequately compensated for by the roof area.
